pr_title: server: support nodes API endpoint for secondary shared tenants
pr_body:
The "nodes" status API endpoint should work with "shared" secondary tenants. Since nodes are common to all the tenants, this API endpoint behaves similar to that of system tenant. Shared service tenants implicitly have all capabilities.

Tenant connector implements TenantStatusServer interface. Status server in secondary tenants make use of tenant connector to fetch nodes information.

Support for external tenants is tracked in a separate ticket.

Fixes: https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/110023
Epic: [CRDB-38968](https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-38968)
Release note (multi-tenancy): The "nodes" endpoint should work for "shared" secondary tenants. Since nodes are common to all the tenants, this API endpoint behaves similar to that of system tenant.

issue_context.title: server: the "nodes" status API endpoint should work with secondary tenants with capability `can_view_node_info`
issue_context.body:
Found while investigating #110001.

**Describe the problem**

When `TestNodeStatusResponse` in `server/storage_api` is modified to point to a secondary tenant (e.g. via #110008), the test starts failing when accessing the `/_status/nodes` endpoint:


```
    nodes_test.go:113: expected privilege error, got status: 501 Not Implemented, content-type: application/json, body: {
          "error": "method Nodes not implemented",
          "code": 12,
          "message": "method Nodes not implemented",
          "details": [
          ]
        }, error: <nil>
```

**How to reproduce**

from #110008 reset `DefaultTestTenant` in `TestNodeStatusResponse`, run the test with a test tenant and observe the failure.

**Expected behavior**

Once the tenant is granted a suitable capability, the endpoint should work properly. It should retrieve the node details over the KV tenant connector over the network.

Epic CRDB-38968



Jira issue: CRDB-31228
comments: NB: the test `TestNodesGRPCResponse` is also affected.

@dhartunian (or @stevendanna if you have opinions on this) I've a small clarification for this and related issues like https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/110019 and https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/issues/110018. Do we want to show nodes, ranges and range/{id} only for that particular tenant or should it behave just like system tenant behind an appropriate capability?

It seems intuitive to limit to that particular tenant but I need a product confirmation before going ahead as that may decide technical details.

@shubhamdhama I think it should behave like the system tenant since we can't really partition "node" information by tenant. This information is used to populate the overview page in DB Console which doesn't really have a "tenant" view.
Thanks @dhartunian for the clarification. Is this true for all of the other API listed under https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/browse/CRDB-38968 like `range(s)`, `gossip` etc.?

Not quite. I think range information can be partitioned by tenant since the keyspace is tenant-scoped, but, for instance, "gossip" is a node-to-node system and has no tenant-level meaning.

Looking at the API list in the epic, I think only range-related stuff should be partitioned, the rest of the items are system-tenant node-level data.

`_status/nodes` endpoint was not implemented by `statusServer` which is used by secondary tenants. With changes in https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/pull/131644, `_status/nodes` and `_status/nodes/{node-id}` endpoints work with secondary _shared_ tenants. Since nodes are shared by all secondary tenants, the behavior of these endpoints is similar to that of system tenant.

_External_ tenants only run SQL instances. Node information must be fetched using RPC calls. To enable `_status/nodes` and `_status/nodes/{node-id}`, `statusServer` implementation must be modified to make an RPC call using tenant connector. 

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/d183df0301b3221b145780b73a1eb0052fb0a016/pkg/server/status.go#L1864-L1876

Similarly, profile (CPU, Heap) endpoints are also broken for _external_ tenants. In case of _external_ tenants, these endpoints should allow collecting profiles from SQL instances too. We may (most likely) need new endpoints to support such functionality. We have to spend sometime thinking about the user experience before implementing them for _external_ secondary tenants.

cc: @stevendanna, @dhartunian

review_comments: Thanks for adding this test. 500 for a permissions error is sad, but that is an existing problem that I think we have an issue for somewhere.
Do we have a test that covers that this endpoint fails without the capability? If not, it may be worth it to add one.

I was using the test mentioned in the ticket that was failing before my changes. I tried fixing the test to work for negative case too but found out `can_view_node_info` has no affect on shared tenants. I tested the changes for "external" secondary tenants and it was works as expected. 

On digging further, I found https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/75a1f36daeebcaa1bf9333f1912b83c2b7a54472/pkg/multitenant/tenantcapabilities/tenantcapabilitiesauthorizer/authorizer.go#L469-L475 

From the above comment it looks like shared tenants implicitly have all capabilities unless we introduce a new mode which I believe will be a bigger change.

Yup, sorry for not being a bit more explicit. I think we can probably write a test that explicitly starts a separate process tenant and then makes this API call.  You can do this either by passing `ExternalTestTenantAlwaysEnabled` as the value of `DefaultTestTenant` during TestServer startup, or by passing `TestControlsTenantsExplicitly` and then using the methods on TestServer to start a separate process test server manually.  Putting this test in place in the server package will probably be useful as we can add more of these negative cases to it as we enable more endpoints.

https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/b617593ae2d5013035b3633f95c585948471d2d3/pkg/server/storage_api/nodes_test.go#L93-L103
I created the negative test for external tenant using a table. Let me know if you prefer a separate test for the external mode.
